title: ephemeral-egress-buffer-and-transparent-slowpath-stabilizer
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: incidents in multiple regions showed repeated short-lived egress saturation causing aggressive regional evacuations which then amplified latency spikes. This PR introduces an ephemeral egress buffer and a transparent slowpath stabilizer to reduce evacuation churn and give SLO enforcement a short, telemetry-driven backoff window. Design summary: (1) egress-buffer: lightweight in-memory token reservoir per node that absorbs microbursts and provides a small grace window before triggering full regional evacuation; capacity is proportional to recent egress velocity and tenant pressure. (2) slowpath-stabilizer: a short-lived soft-circuit state that defers hard circuit flips for requests matching transparent-evict criteria (inflight KV pressure or short TTL tenants). (3) telemetry hooks: new metrics exposed to tracing and Console (node.egress.buffer_fill, tenant.evacuations_deferred, stabilizer.reopens) and an emergency rollback flag under feature-gates. Hotfix constraints: default-off feature gate enabled for affected clusters via Canary rollout, strict guardrails (max deferral 5s, global cap), and an automatic decay to avoid masking real capacity issues. Rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 (5% nodes) -> gradual 25% -> full region -> cross-region rollouts only after 48h stable. Link to incident: SUP-4432. Checklist: automated unit + integration tests added, load-runner scenario replayed against recorded traces, manual canary validation runbook attached. Commits and scope are intentionally focused to keep revert simple.

review_comments: Jared Ortiz: Overall approach looks good; two asks: (1) add a prometheus label to tenant.evacuations_deferred to allow slicing by tenant-id, (2) ensure the max_deferral is configurable at runtime for hotpatching.
Aisha Kumar: Addressed both; added tenant label and runtime-config via /internal/config/feature_flags. Updated telemetry docs accordingly.
Maya Chen: Found a potential race in EvacuationController when both buffer drain and node drain race; suggest adding a node-level mutex or CAS.
Aisha Kumar: Added CAS guard and a stress test that reproduces the original race locally (tests/stabilizer_integration_test.go).
Luca Romano: CI flaky test observed once; reran and passed. Recommend merge after canary validation policy is in place.
qa_and_testing: Unit tests covering allocator edge cases and capacity decay
Load-runner scenario simulating 10k rps microbursts with mixed tenants
Manual canary verification checklist (latency, eviction-rate, telemetry drift)
known_risks: If global cap misconfigured, deferral could mask a real sustained outage — mitigated by max_global_defer and automatic decay
Telemetry sampling delay could under-report buffer burn; dashboards updated with a high-cardinality hook
Edge case: tenants with very long TTLs may not fall under the transparent slowpath and still be evacuated (expected behavior)
rollback_plan: Flip feature-gate canary-egress-buffer: false -> immediate disable of soft deferrals
Rolling restart not required; controller reads gate dynamically, change takes effect within 2s
If downstream instability persists, revert commit f2c7d4a and redeploy (documented emergency revert steps)
operational_notes: New metrics: node.egress.buffer_fill, node.egress.buffer_capacity, tenant.evacuations_deferred, stabilizer.hold_count
Alert tuning: add alert if tenant.evacuations_deferred spikes > 100/min for 5m
Console: added a small op-runbook under Docs -> Operations -> egress-buffer.md
merge_outcome: merged via squash merge to main after canary gating and CI rerun
release_notes: Introduces an ephemeral egress buffer and transparent slowpath stabilizer to reduce short-lived regional evacuations and lower latency spikes during microbursts. Enabled via feature gate and rolled out via canary.
Adds new telemetry for buffer fill and deferred evacuations. Ops: see docs/ops/egress-buffer.md for verification steps.
